deities: Ram Lalla (Balak Ram, the child form of Rama)

history.period: Contemporary (bhoomi pujan 5 August 2020; pran pratishtha 22 January 2024)
history.summary: Hindu tradition holds the site to be Ram Janmabhoomi, the birthplace of Rama. The site was the former location of the Babri Masjid (built c. 1529), demolished in 1992; in a 2019 judgement the Supreme Court awarded the disputed site to Hindus for a temple and allotted land in Dhannipur to Muslims for a mosque. Prime Minister Narendra Modi performed the bhoomi pujan on 5 August 2020 and the pran pratishtha of Ram Lalla on 22 January 2024. Built in Nagara style by the Sompura family of architects under the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, the temple is 380 ft long, 250 ft wide and 161 ft tall with 392 carved pillars, pink Bansi Paharpur sandstone with no iron or steel, and a Makrana-marble-lined garbhagriha housing the Ram Lalla idol (Balak Ram) carved from Karnataka's Krishna Shila. A CBRI Roorkee optical system projects sunlight onto Ram Lalla's forehead at noon on Ram Navami (Surya Tilak). The complex received further consecrations (Raja Ram and other deities in eight satellite temples) on 5 June 2025. NOTE: temple complex construction was still ongoing into 2025; hours and facilities may change - verify with the Trust.

name: Ram Janmabhoomi Temple
town_description: Ayodhya is an ancient city on the Saryu river in Uttar Pradesh, one of the seven most sacred pilgrimage cities (Sapta Puri) of Hinduism and, by tradition, the capital of the Kosala kingdom and birthplace of Rama. Renamed from Faizabad in 2018, it is now a major pilgrimage destination with its own international airport and has become one of the most visited religious sites in the world.

travel.airport: Maharshi Valmiki International Airport, Ayodhya (~15 km); Lucknow Airport (~135 km)
travel.road: NH 27 connects Ayodhya to Lucknow (135 km) and Varanasi (200 km); buses run from Lucknow, Agra and major cities.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Ram Navami (Surya Tilak at 12:00 noon) is the biggest event but draws extreme crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: General darshan 7:00 AM-11:30 AM and 2:00 PM-7:00 PM daily; sanctum closed 12:00 PM-2:00 PM for Bhog. Aartis: Mangala 4:00 AM, Shringar 6:30 AM, Sandhya 7:00 PM, Shayan 9:30 PM (aarti passes required). Free Sugam Darshan e-pass at online.srjbtkshetra.org; slots release at midnight 15 days ahead. No paid VIP darshan exists (beware agents).
